primary.title: The Speeches of Queen Elizabeth I
primary.author: Elizabeth I of England
primary.rationale: Collection of her most famous speeches, including the Tilbury speech, offering direct insight into her rhetoric and political messaging.

primary.title: Elizabeth I: Collected Works
primary.author: Elizabeth I of England
primary.rationale: A comprehensive academic collection of her letters, speeches, poems, and prayers, providing a broad view of her intellectual and political life. While the collection is modern, the individual works are primary.

primary.title: Letters of Queen Elizabeth I
primary.author: Elizabeth I of England
primary.rationale: A selection of her correspondence, revealing her diplomatic dealings, personal relationships, and administrative concerns.

secondary.title: Elizabeth I
secondary.author: David Starkey
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded biography by a prominent Tudor historian, offering a detailed and scholarly analysis of her reign and personality.

secondary.title: The Faces of Elizabeth I
secondary.author: Lisa M. Bitel
secondary.rationale: Examines Elizabeth's image and self-representation through various lenses, including portraiture, propaganda, and her own writings, providing a nuanced scholarly perspective.

secondary.title: Elizabeth I and Her Parliaments, 1559-1581
secondary.author: J.E. Neale
secondary.rationale: While slightly before the 1976 cutoff, this is a foundational scholarly work on Elizabeth's relationship with Parliament. A later volume covers 1581-1603.

suggestions.notes: The 'Collected Works' and 'Letters' are modern compilations of primary source material. The 'Speeches' are also typically found in collections. Neale's work is included as a highly influential precursor to later scholarship, though it predates the 1976 requirement.
